examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A variable is live if some future path uses its current value before redefining it. Solve backward with OUT=union of successor IN sets and IN=USE∪(OUT−DEF). Back edges can keep variables live across blocks even when the exit path uses nothing. Liveness supports dead-code removal and register interference analysis.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Block contains x=a+b; y=x+c and exits where only y is live. How many variables are live at block entry?

**Answer: 3.** Work backward: before y=x+c, x and c are needed; before x=a+b, its old x is killed and a,b are needed. Entry set is {a,b,c}, of size 3. y's old value is not needed.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An assignment can be removed only if its result is dead and evaluating it has no required side effects or exceptions under the chosen semantics.

Dead variable values and unreachable control-flow blocks are different forms of dead code.
